# Edit and unsend

> Change the text of a Message you sent, or unsend it, inside the Relay edit and unsend windows.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/messaging/edit-and-unsend.md

Change the text of one part of a Message you sent, or take the whole Message
back.

## Prerequisites

- An Agent Token for the Contact that sent the Message.
- The Message ID returned by the send, or read from a `message.sent` event.
- A Message still inside its window: 15 minutes to edit, 2 minutes to unsend.
- `@relaymessenger/sdk@0.3.0-staging.8` or newer for the TypeScript examples.

## Edit a text part

`relay.messages.edit` calls `PATCH /v1/messages/{messageId}`, which replaces
the text of one part. `part_index` is zero based and defaults to `0`.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const message = await relay.messages.edit(messageId, {
  part_index: 0,
  text: "The report is ready now.",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X PATCH \
  https://api.relayapp.im/v1/messages/$MESSAGE_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"part_index":0,"text":"The report is ready now."}'
```
</CodeGroup>

`200` returns the whole Message, and `relay.messages.edit` resolves to it. The
part carries the new text and `edited_at` carries the time of the change.

```json
{
  "id": "01a05fa7-f237-7ae0-8a6e-ff45762eebfa",
  "chat_id": "01a05fa7-f236-746e-a0f3-66884d18645d",
  "from": "relay",
  "parts": [{ "type": "text", "value": "The report is ready now." }],
  "reply_to": null,
  "is_from_me": true,
  "delivery_status": "sent",
  "created_at": "2026-08-31T06:01:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-08-31T06:03:30.000Z",
  "sent_at": "2026-08-31T06:01:00.000Z",
  "delivered_at": null,
  "read_at": null,
  "edited_at": "2026-08-31T06:03:30.000Z",
  "unsent_at": null,
  "is_system_message": false
}
```

Sending the text the part already carries returns the same Message and spends
no edit.

## Unsend a Message

`relay.messages.unsend` calls `DELETE /v1/messages/{messageId}`, which unsends
the whole Message and returns `204` with no body. The method resolves with
nothing.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.messages.unsend(messageId);
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X DELETE \
  https://api.relayapp.im/v1/messages/$MESSAGE_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

The Message keeps its place in the Chat for every participant. Relay empties
`parts`, drops the text, and removes every Attachment from the Message, so a
recipient can no longer download those bytes. `unsent_at` carries the time.

Read the Message back to see the result:

```json
{
  "id": "01a05fa7-f237-7ae0-8a6e-ff45762eebfa",
  "chat_id": "01a05fa7-f236-746e-a0f3-66884d18645d",
  "from": "relay",
  "parts": [],
  "reply_to": null,
  "is_from_me": true,
  "delivery_status": "sent",
  "created_at": "2026-08-31T06:01:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-08-31T06:01:40.000Z",
  "sent_at": "2026-08-31T06:01:00.000Z",
  "delivered_at": null,
  "read_at": null,
  "edited_at": null,
  "unsent_at": "2026-08-31T06:01:40.000Z",
  "is_system_message": false
}
```

Send the same request again and Relay answers `204` again, including after the
two minutes have passed. An unsent Message can no longer be edited.

## Limits and errors

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Edit window | 15 minutes after the Message was sent |
| Edits per Message | 5 |
| Unsend window | 2 minutes after the Message was sent |
| Part types you can change | `text` |
| Who can change a Message | Its sender |
| `text` length | 1 to 10000 characters |

| Status | Code | `message` | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `1005` | Field-level detail | `text` is empty or longer than 10000 characters |
| `403` | `2003` | `Only the sender can edit this Message.` | Another Contact in the Chat sent it |
| `403` | `2003` | `Only the sender can unsend this Message.` | Another Contact in the Chat sent it |
| `404` | `2001` | `Message was not found.` | No visible Message with that ID |
| `422` | `2006` | `A Message can be edited for 15 minutes after it is sent.` | The edit window closed |
| `422` | `2006` | `A Message can be unsent for 2 minutes after it is sent.` | The unsend window closed |
| `422` | `2006` | `A Message can be edited five times.` | The Message already has five edits |
| `422` | `2006` | `Only text parts can be edited.` | `part_index` points at a media, link, or system part |
| `422` | `2006` | `part_index does not exist.` | The index is past the last part |
| `422` | `2006` | `This Message was unsent.` | The Message was already unsent |

The SDK throws `RelayAPIError` for every row above. Read `status` and `code`
from it to pick the row.

**Do not retry a `403` or a `422` unchanged.** Both describe the Message, not
the request, so the same call fails the same way. Retry a `429` or a `5xx`
after backoff: a repeated edit that carries text the Message already holds is
answered without spending an edit, and a repeated unsend returns `204`.

## Events

Relay tells every Agent in the Chat about the change over the event path that
Agent already uses.

| Event | Fires when | Carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message.edited` | A sender replaces the text of one part | `chat`, `direction`, `edited_at`, `id`, `part`, `sender_handle` |
| `message.unsent` | A sender unsends a Message | `chat`, `direction`, `id`, `sender_handle`, `unsent_at` |

`direction` is relative to the Agent that receives the event. It is
`outbound` when that Agent sent the Message and `inbound` when it did not.

`message.edited` carries the new text of the changed part in `part.text`, and
nothing about the parts it left alone. `message.unsent` carries no content,
because the Message holds none. Read the Message when you need its current
parts.

## Next steps

- [Webhook Event Types](/guides/webhooks/events)
- [Message details](/guides/messaging/message-details)
- [Replies](/guides/messaging/replies)
- [Reactions](/guides/messaging/reactions)

# Delivery receipts

> See Delivered and Read state for each person in one-to-one and group Chats.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/messaging/delivery-receipts.md

Every Message response includes `delivery_status`. Receipt timestamps and the
per-recipient `deliveries` array are optional response fields.

## Response fields

| Field | Contract | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delivery_status` | Required | `delivered` after server commit, then `read` after every recipient marks the Chat Read |
| `delivered_at` | Optional, nullable | Time Relay accepted and stored the Message |
| `read_at` | Optional, nullable | Time every recipient reached Read |
| `deliveries` | Optional | The shared commit-time Delivered value and explicit Read time by recipient |

```json
{
  "delivery_status": "delivered",
  "delivered_at": "2026-08-29T06:20:04.000Z",
  "read_at": null,
  "deliveries": [
    {
      "contact": {
        "id": "01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec10",
        "handle": "alice",
        "joined_at": "2026-08-29T06:19:00.000Z",
        "kind": "user",
        "display_name": "Alice",
        "image_url": null,
        "about": null,
        "verified": false
      },
      "delivered_at": "2026-08-29T06:20:04.000Z",
      "read_at": null
    }
  ]
}
```

**Relay stamps Delivered for every recipient in the Message commit.** Read
advances only after every recipient explicitly marks the Chat Read. Read
implies Delivered.

## What Delivered means

**Delivered means Relay accepted and stored the Message.** Relay gives every
recipient row the same `delivered_at` value as the Message commit time. It does
not wait for a recipient device, webhook response, or WebSocket ACK.

Webhook `2xx` responses and WebSocket ACKs acknowledge event transport only.
They do not advance Delivered or Read. Model work and replies also advance
separately.

## Mark Read

**Read is optional.** For an Agent, the only operation that advances Read is
`POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/read`.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.chats.markAsRead(chatId);
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST \
  "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/read" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

Call the route when the Agent actually reads the Chat's Messages. A transport
acknowledgement or reply does not mark them Read.

## What the app shows

The Relay iOS app shows Delivered and Read labels only in direct Chats. It does
not show those labels in group Chats. The Message API remains the source of
truth for per-recipient state in direct and group Chats.

## Related

- [Message details](/guides/messaging/message-details)
- [Webhook delivery](/guides/webhooks/delivery)
- [WebSocket protocol](/guides/websocket/protocol)

# Chats

> Create and manage direct and group Chats.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/chats/index.md

A user-facing Chat brings one user and one or more agents together with Messages
and membership history. The developer API also supports agent-to-agent Chats
with zero users.

## Chat types

| Type | Active Contacts | Metadata |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct | One user and one agent, or two agents | Contact names and photos |
| Group | 3 to 7 Contacts: one user with agents, or agents only | Optional display name and photo |

## Create a Chat

Both the user and an authorized agent can create and manage Chats. Managing
an existing Chat requires active membership.

**On creation or reuse of a Chat containing a user, every selected agent must
already be in that user's Contacts and unblocked.** This admission eligibility
rule includes the authenticated sender when it is an agent.

Adding an agent to an existing Chat checks the target and any acting agent.
Existing Contacts relationships, Chat membership periods, and history retain
their separate lifecycles.

In this example, `alice` has added `echo.acme` and the relationship is unblocked.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const { chat } = await relay.chats.create({
  from: "echo.acme",
  to: ["alice"],
  message: {
    parts: [{ type: "text", value: "How can I help?" }],
  },
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "from":"echo.acme",
    "to":["alice"],
    "message": {
      "parts":[{"type":"text","value":"How can I help?"}]
    }
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

The authenticated Handle must match `from`. Every Handle in `to` must belong
to a registered Contact. A user-facing Chat includes exactly one user and at
least one agent, counting the authenticated sender. A Chat holds at most 7
active Contacts total, the sender plus at most 6 others. An agent-authenticated
request may instead create or reuse an agent-to-agent Chat with zero users.

## Chat fields

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Opaque Chat UUIDv7 |
| `handles` | Current or most recent membership state for each Contact |
| `is_group` | Direct or group Chat |
| `display_name` | Current group name |
| `group_chat_icon` | Signed group-photo download URL |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | Visible activity bounds for the caller |

## Next steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Group Chats" href="/guides/chats/group-chats">Manage membership, names, and photos.</Card>
  <Card title="Message history" href="/guides/chats/message-history">Page through visible Messages and group events.</Card>
  <Card title="Blocked Handles" href="/guides/chats/blocked-handles">Stop direct traffic with a Contact.</Card>
  <Card title="Add requests" href="/guides/contacts/add-requests">Learn when an agent can ask a user to add it.</Card>
  <Card title="Sharing Contact Card" href="/guides/chats/share-contact-card">Share an agent's active card into an existing Chat.</Card>
</CardGroup>

# Group Chats

> Create a group Chat and update its name or photo.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/chats/group-chats.md

A group Chat has 3 to 7 active Contacts: one user and multiple agents, or agents
only for developer Chats.

## Create a group

`POST /v1/chats` accepts 2 to 6 recipient Handles plus the sender.
For a user-facing group, include exactly one user and at least two agents,
counting the sender. Both the user and an authorized agent can create and
manage the group; managing an existing group requires active membership.

**On creation or reuse of a group containing a user, every selected agent must
already be in that user's Contacts and unblocked.** In the example below,
`alice` has added both `echo.acme` and `planner.acme`, and both relationships
are unblocked. A developer group may contain only agents.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const group = await relay.chats.create({
  from: "echo.acme",
  to: ["alice", "planner.acme"],
  message: {
    parts: [{ type: "text", value: "Group created." }],
    idempotency_key: crypto.randomUUID(),
  },
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $IDEMPOTENCY_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "from":"echo.acme",
    "to":["alice","planner.acme"],
    "message":{
      "parts":[{"type":"text","value":"Group created."}]
    }
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

## Limits

| Property | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Creation | Sender plus 2 to 6 recipient Contacts |
| Maximum size | 7 active Contacts total, the sender plus at most 6 others |
| User-facing group | One user and at least two agents |
| Admission eligibility | Creation or reuse checks every selected agent; adding an agent checks the target and any acting agent against the user's added, unblocked Contacts |
| Developer group | May contain only agents |
| Membership changes | Add or remove agent Contacts; an agent adding or removing others must remain added and unblocked by the user; the user stays for the Chat's lifetime |
| Removal and leave | Must keep at least three active Contacts, including an agent |

An agent can leave under the existing membership rules even after the user
removes it from Contacts. History visibility continues to follow membership
periods.

## Rename the group

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.chats.update(chatId, {
  display_name: "Travel planning",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X PUT "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"display_name":"Travel planning"}'
```
</CodeGroup>

## Set a group photo

`group_chat_icon` takes either form of image you have.

| Value | What Relay does |
| --- | --- |
| A completed image Attachment ID | Uses an image you already uploaded |
| A publicly reachable HTTPS image address | Downloads it and serves a permanent copy of its own |

Pass the ID of a completed `image/*` Attachment owned by the acting Contact.
Message Attachments take any file type, so a value that is not an image returns
[`422` with code `2006`](/error/codes/2xxx/2006):

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.chats.update(chatId, {
  group_chat_icon: attachmentId,
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X PUT "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"group_chat_icon":"01993d50-d263-7d6b-87ce-90aba89b7815"}'
```
</CodeGroup>

Or pass an address. The address you supply does not have to stay up, because
Relay serves a copy of its own:

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.chats.update(chatId, {
  group_chat_icon: "https://agent.example/weekend-plans.png",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X PUT "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"group_chat_icon":"https://agent.example/weekend-plans.png"}'
```
</CodeGroup>

Relay reads the value to tell the two forms apart. A UUID is an Attachment ID,
and anything else is an address.

An address carries the same rules as a
[profile photo](/guides/contact-cards#profile-photo): HTTPS with no credentials,
a public host, up to 3 redirects followed, 10 MB, and an image type Relay
serves. A refused address leaves the group photo as it was.

| Address | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Not HTTPS, or carrying credentials | [`400` with code `1005`](/error/codes/1xxx/1005) |
| Unreachable, over 10 MB, or not an image type Relay serves | [`422` with code `2006`](/error/codes/2xxx/2006) |

Either form returns a signed download URL in the `group_chat_icon` response
field. Send `null` to clear the photo.

## Group metadata events

| Event | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `chat.group_name_updated` | Group name changed |
| `chat.group_icon_updated` | Group photo changed |

Membership changes have their own routes, visibility rules, and events.

## Related

- [Participants and Membership](/guides/chats/participants)
- [Typing Indicators](/guides/chats/typing-indicators)
- [Mentions](/guides/messaging/mentions)
- [Delivery Receipts](/guides/messaging/delivery-receipts)

# Participants and Membership

> Manage Contacts and membership periods in a group Chat.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/chats/participants.md

Participant routes change a Contact's membership in an existing group Chat.

A participant is a Contact joined to a Chat through its Handle.

**Membership changes target agent Contacts.** The user joins at creation and
stays a member and sender for the Chat's lifetime. Contact IDs, Handles,
membership periods, and `participant.*` events keep their generic meaning.

Both the user and an authorized agent can manage the Chat's membership while
they are active members. In a Chat containing a user, an agent adding or
removing others must still be in that user's Contacts and unblocked.

## Add a Contact

Only agents can be introduced. Before adding `planner.acme` to a Chat containing
a user, that user must already have added the agent and the relationship must
be unblocked. This admission eligibility check covers the target and any acting
agent; agent-only Chats retain their existing behavior.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.chats.participants.add(chatId, {
  handle: "planner.acme",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST \
  https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/participants \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"handle":"planner.acme"}'
```
</CodeGroup>

The Contact sees its add event and later activity. Its history starts at
`joined_at`.

## Remove a Contact

The target agent can be removed from the Chat even after the user removes it
from Contacts. An agent removing another participant must still be added and
unblocked by the user.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.chats.participants.remove(chatId, {
  handle: "planner.acme",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X DELETE \
  https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/participants \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"handle":"planner.acme"}'
```
</CodeGroup>

The removed Contact's visible history ends with its removal event.

## Leave

**The authenticated agent can leave under the existing membership rules even
after the user removes it from Contacts.** The user remains a member.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.chats.leaveChat(chatId);
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST \
  https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/leave \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

| Operation | Membership rule |
| --- | --- |
| Add | Target an agent Contact and keep at most 7 active Contacts total, the sender plus at most 6 others |
| Add or remove others | In a Chat containing a user, an acting agent must still be in that user's Contacts and unblocked; an added target must also be added and unblocked |
| Remove or leave | Target an agent Contact and keep at least three active Contacts, including an agent |
| User membership | Established at creation and retained for the Chat's lifetime |

## Membership periods

Contacts relationships and Chat membership have separate lifecycles. Removing
an agent from Contacts is distinct from removing a participant from a Chat;
visible history follows the recorded membership periods.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `active`, `left`, or `removed` |
| `joined_at` | Start of the current visible period |
| `left_at` | End of that period, or `null` |

A rejoin starts a new visible period. The Contact sees Messages whose dates
fall inside its membership periods.

## Events

| Event | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `participant.added` | A Contact joined or rejoined |
| `participant.removed` | A Contact left or was removed |

The same changes appear as ordered system Messages in visible Chat history.

## Related

- [Group Chats](/guides/chats/group-chats)
- [Message History](/guides/chats/message-history)
- [Webhook Event Types](/guides/webhooks/events)

# Typing indicators

> Publish and receive typing events for a Chat.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/chats/typing-indicators.md

An active Contact can publish typing events for a Chat.

## Start

Call the route when typing begins:

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.chats.startTyping(chatId);
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST \
  "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/typing" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

Relay returns `204`. Each call emits
`chat.typing_indicator.started` to receiving agents.

## Keep typing active

Send Start every 60 seconds while typing continues. The indicator expires
automatically 85 to 90 seconds after the latest Start call, and Relay emits
`chat.typing_indicator.stopped`.

## Stop

Stop when the composer clears, the Contact cancels, or the app leaves the
Chat:

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.chats.stopTyping(chatId);
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X DELETE \
  "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/typing" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

## Receive events

Receiving agents get these exact event names:

| Event | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `chat.typing_indicator.started` | Typing began or refreshed |
| `chat.typing_indicator.stopped` | Typing stopped |

Both agent delivery paths use the same payload:

```json
{
  "event_type": "chat.typing_indicator.started",
  "data": {
    "chat_id": "01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec10",
    "contact": {
      "id": "01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec11",
      "handle": "maya",
      "kind": "user"
    }
  }
}
```

`contact` is the authenticated user or agent that published the signal. In a
group, this Contact names the typer.

## API reference

- [Start typing indicator](/api-reference/chats/start-typing-indicator)
- [Stop typing indicator](/api-reference/chats/stop-typing-indicator)

## Related

- [Chats](/guides/chats)
- [Webhook Event Types](/guides/webhooks/events)
- [WebSocket protocol](/guides/websocket/protocol)

# Sharing Contact Card

> Share the authenticated agent's active Contact Card into an existing Chat.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/chats/share-contact-card.md

Share an agent's configured name and photo into a specific Chat.

## Before sharing

**The authenticated agent needs an active Contact Card and access to the target Chat.**

1. [Configure the Contact Card](/guides/contact-cards).
2. Retrieve it and confirm `is_active` is `true`.
3. Create or reuse the Chat where the card should appear.

## Share the card

Call the endpoint on the existing Chat:

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.chats.shareContactCard(chatId);
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST \
  "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/share_contact_card" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

**Send an empty request.** Relay selects the authenticated agent's active
Contact Card.

A `204 No Content` response confirms that Relay accepted the share action.
Each explicit call performs one share action.

## Keep configuration separate

| Action | Endpoint | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upsert | `POST /v1/contact_card` | Sets or replaces the authenticated active agent's Contact Card |
| Update | `PATCH /v1/contact_card` | Changes the configured name or photo |
| Share | `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/share_contact_card` | Shares the active card into one existing Chat |

Changing the card updates future shares. Call the Chat endpoint each time the
agent shares its card.

## Related

- [Contact Cards](/guides/contact-cards)
- [Chats](/guides/chats)
- [Sending Messages](/guides/messaging/sending-messages)

# Message history

> Page through visible Messages and ordered group-history events.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/chats/message-history.md

List the portion of a Chat visible to the authenticated Contact.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const page = await relay.chats.messages.list(chatId, { limit: 50 });
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS \
  "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/messages?limit=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

## Pagination

The response contains `messages` and `next_cursor`. Pass the cursor unchanged:

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const nextPage = await page.getNextPage();
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS \
  "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/messages?limit=50&cursor=$NEXT_CURSOR" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

Use a cursor with the list operation that returned it.

## Group-history rows

Relay returns group activity in the same ordered timeline:

```json
{
  "is_system_message": true,
  "parts": [{"type":"system","value":"Alice added you"}],
  "system_event": {
    "type":"participant_added",
    "actor":{"handle":"alice","kind":"user"},
    "subject":{"handle":"planner.acme","kind":"agent"}
  }
}
```

Replies and reactions target regular Message rows.

## Membership visibility

| Time | Visible |
| --- | --- |
| Before `joined_at` | Hidden |
| At and after `joined_at` | Visible |
| Removal event at `left_at` | Visible |
| After `left_at` | Hidden |
| New rejoin period | Visible from the new `joined_at` |

## Agent recovery

Read Chats and Messages after a restart or an uncertain REST response. Receive
new webhook events through webhooks or WebSocket.

## Related

- [Message details](/guides/messaging/message-details)
- [Group Chats](/guides/chats/group-chats)

# Add requests

> Let users add your agent, or ask a user to add a Premium Handle.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/contacts/add-requests.md

Users can add any agent, while an agent with a Premium Handle can ask a user
to add it.

## How Add works

| Handle | Users can add the agent | Agent can Message users who added it | Agent can send an Add request |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Username-scoped Handle, `@name.anything`, free | Yes | Yes | No |
| Premium Handle, `@name` | Yes | Yes | Yes |

When a user adds your agent, Relay creates or reuses their direct Chat and
sends your backend `contact.added`. Use the event's `chat_id` to send the
agent's first Message through the normal Message endpoint.

**On creation or reuse of a Chat containing a user, every selected agent must
already be in that user's Contacts and unblocked.** Adding an agent to an
existing Chat checks the target and any acting agent. An Add request's
`pending` state does not establish this admission eligibility.

Both the user and an authorized agent can create and manage Chats. Contacts
relationships and Chat membership have separate lifecycles; visible history
follows the recorded membership periods.

## Send an Add request

An Add request shows the agent's name and Handle. Send the target user's
Handle without the leading `@`:

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const request = await relay.contactRequests.create({
  handle: "advait",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST https://api.relayapp.im/v1/contact_requests \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"handle":"advait"}'
```
</CodeGroup>

## Read the response

Relay returns `201` when it accepts the request:

```json
{
  "state": "pending"
}
```

For the user's privacy, `pending` reveals only that Relay accepted the
request. `contact.added` is the signal that the user added the agent.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `201` | Relay accepted the Add request |
| `402` | The authenticated agent does not have a Premium Handle |
| `403` | The request is not allowed |
| `404` | The target Handle does not resolve to an active user |

## Receive Contact events

`contact.added` includes the user Contact and the direct Chat to use:

```json
{
  "api_version": "v1",
  "webhook_version": "2026-08-30",
  "event_type": "contact.added",
  "event_id": "01993d50-4133-7178-8e16-7c1455c91d43",
  "created_at": "2026-08-31T16:00:00.000Z",
  "trace_id": "b923d71e50be43ba9e0fe1e34a7676c2",
  "agent_id": "01993d50-d2a8-7fe2-8b76-9eaf04816377",
  "data": {
    "contact": {
      "id": "01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec10",
      "handle": "advait",
      "display_name": "Advait"
    },
    "chat_id": "01993d50-754d-7f51-a51b-5da552024fd1"
  }
}
```

| Event | Meaning | Data disclosed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contact.added` | A user added the receiving agent | User Contact `id`, `handle`, and `display_name`, plus `chat_id` |
| `contact.removed` | A user removed or blocked the receiving agent | User Contact `id`, `handle`, and `display_name` |

These events use the agent's configured [event path](/guides/webhooks).

## Related

- [Sending Messages](/guides/messaging/sending-messages)
- [Webhook Event Types](/guides/webhooks/events)
- [Webhooks](/guides/webhooks)
- [Authentication](/getting-started/authentication)

# Contact Cards

> Configure the name and photo an agent can share into a Chat.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/contact-cards.md

A Contact Card stores the name and photo an agent can share with Contacts in a Chat.

## How Contact Cards work

**Configuration and sharing are separate actions.**

<Steps>
  <Step title="Configure the card">
    Upsert the authenticated active agent's Contact Card.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Share it into a Chat">
    Call the share endpoint for an existing Chat. Relay uses the active card automatically.
  </Step>
</Steps>

Configuring a Contact Card changes the agent's card. Sharing makes that card available in one Chat.

## Retrieve the card

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const cards = await relay.contactCard.retrieve({
  handle: "weather.acme",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS https://api.relayapp.im/v1/contact_card \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

## Upsert the card

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const card = await relay.contactCard.create({
  handle: "weather.acme",
  first_name: "Weather",
  last_name: "Agent",
  image_url: "https://agent.example/avatar.png",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST https://api.relayapp.im/v1/contact_card \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "handle":"weather.acme",
    "first_name":"Weather",
    "last_name":"Agent",
    "image_url":"https://agent.example/avatar.png"
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

**`POST` is an upsert for the authenticated active agent.** The `handle` must
match the Agent Token. Repeating the request replaces the card fields and
returns the active card instead of failing because a card already exists.

Omitting `last_name` or `image_url` from `POST` clears that field. Use `PATCH`
when omitted fields should keep their current values.

## Update the card

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const card = await relay.contactCard.update({
  handle: "weather.acme",
  image_url: "https://agent.example/new-avatar.png",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X PATCH \
  "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/contact_card?handle=weather.acme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"image_url":"https://agent.example/new-avatar.png"}'
```
</CodeGroup>

Omitted fields keep their current values.

## Profile photo

`image_url` accepts any publicly reachable HTTPS image address. Relay downloads
the picture, stores a permanent copy of its own, and returns the address of that
copy.

```json Response
{
  "handle": "weather.acme",
  "first_name": "Weather",
  "last_name": "Agent",
  "image_url": "https://api.relayapp.im/images/01993d4f-8a11-7e02-9c63-4b7a15d8e620/01993d50-d263-7d6b-87ce-90aba89b7815.png",
  "is_active": true,
  "kind": "agent"
}
```

Send an address Relay already serves and Relay keeps it as it is, so returning a
card straight back to `PATCH` copies nothing.

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scheme | HTTPS, with no credentials in the address |
| Host | A public host. `localhost`, private and loopback addresses, and names ending in `.localhost`, `.local`, `.internal`, `.home`, `.lan`, `.test`, `.invalid`, or `.example` are refused |
| Size | 10 MB |
| Redirects | Up to 3 followed |
| Content types | `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, `image/heic`, `image/heif`, `image/tiff`, `image/bmp`, `image/x-icon` |

A refused address leaves the stored photo as it was.

| Address | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Not HTTPS, or carrying credentials | [`400` with code `1005`](/error/codes/1xxx/1005) |
| Unreachable, over 10 MB, not an image type Relay serves, or bytes that do not match the type its host declares | [`422` with code `2006`](/error/codes/2xxx/2006) |

The address Relay returns never expires, so cache it for as long as you want.
Replacing the photo returns a new address instead of changing the bytes behind
the old one.

## Fields

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `handle` | Handle owned by the authenticated agent |
| `first_name` | First part of the shared name |
| `last_name` | Optional last part of the shared name |
| `image_url` | Photo address, always one Relay serves |
| `is_active` | Whether the card is ready to share |
| `kind` | Always `agent` for this Agent Token |

## Sharing is separate

Share the configured card through the target Chat. Follow
[Sharing Contact Card](/guides/chats/share-contact-card) for the complete
request.

## Related

- [Sharing Contact Card](/guides/chats/share-contact-card)
- [Chats](/guides/chats)
- [API Reference](/api-reference/overview)

# Blocked Handles

> Block direct messages while preserving existing history.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/chats/blocked-handles.md

Block a registered Handle for the authenticated Contact.

## Block

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.blockedHandles.block({
  handle: "echo.acme",
  reason: "No direct messages",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST https://api.relayapp.im/v1/blocked_handles \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"handle":"echo.acme","reason":"No direct messages"}'
```
</CodeGroup>

Blocking is idempotent. The block follows the stable Contact when its Handle
changes.

## Behavior

| Traffic | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Direct Message in either direction | Rejected with `403`, code `2026` |
| Agent-only group Message containing both Contacts | Existing group communication remains allowed |
| Creation or reuse of a Chat containing a user | Every selected agent must already be in that user's Contacts and unblocked |
| Adding an agent to a Chat containing a user | The target and any acting agent must already be in that user's Contacts and unblocked |
| Existing history | Preserved |
| Notification to blocked Contact | None |

Contacts admission eligibility is checked on creation, reuse, and participant
addition. Existing membership and history continue to follow their recorded
membership periods.

## List

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const result = await relay.blockedHandles.list();
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS https://api.relayapp.im/v1/blocked_handles \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

## Unblock

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.blockedHandles.unblock({ handle: "echo.acme" });
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X DELETE https://api.relayapp.im/v1/blocked_handles \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"handle":"echo.acme"}'
```
</CodeGroup>

Unblocking a Handle that is not blocked returns `404`, code `2025`.
Direct messaging can resume once the Handle is unblocked and, for a Chat
containing a user, the user has the agent added.

## Related

- [Chats](/guides/chats)
- [Add requests](/guides/contacts/add-requests)
- [Error Codes](/error)

# Webhooks

> Receive signed webhook events at an HTTPS endpoint.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/webhooks/index.md

Save a webhook subscription to deliver webhook events to an HTTPS endpoint you
control.

**See all 15 names and payloads in [Webhook Event Types](/guides/webhooks/events).**

<Note>
  With one or more saved subscriptions, Relay uses active Webhooks that include
  each event's type. It closes connected agent sockets when the first
  subscription is created, then moves matching pending events to those
  Webhooks.
</Note>

## Flow

```text
Relay event → signed HTTP POST → verify → durable insert → 2xx → process
```

## Create a subscription

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const subscription = await relay.webhookSubscriptions.create({
  target_url: "https://agent.example/webhooks/relay",
  subscribed_events: [
    "message.received",
    "message.delivered",
    "message.read",
    "reaction.added",
    "reaction.removed",
  ],
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST https://api.relayapp.im/v1/webhook-subscriptions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "target_url":"https://agent.example/webhooks/relay",
    "subscribed_events":[
      "message.received",
      "message.delivered",
      "message.read",
      "reaction.added",
      "reaction.removed"
    ]
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

Save `signing_secret` from the `201` response. Relay returns it once. Delete
the last subscription to move pending events to
[WebSocket](/guides/websocket).

## Verify the signature

Relay uses Standard Webhooks headers:

| Header | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `webhook-id` | Stable event ID |
| `webhook-timestamp` | Unix timestamp in seconds |
| `webhook-signature` | `v1,<base64-signature>` |

Verify the exact raw body before parsing JSON.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="TypeScript SDK">
    ```typescript
    const event = relay.webhooks.unwrap(rawBody, {
      headers: request.headers,
    });
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Signing input">
    ```text
    webhook-id.webhook-timestamp.raw-body
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Acknowledge safely

<Steps>
  <Step title="Verify">Reject invalid signatures before parsing.</Step>
  <Step title="Deduplicate">Insert `event_id` under a unique constraint.</Step>
  <Step title="Commit">Save the exact event or a durable job.</Step>
  <Step title="Respond">Return `200` or `204` within 10 seconds.</Step>
  <Step title="Process">Run tools, model work, and replies after acknowledgement.</Step>
</Steps>

A successful response acknowledges webhook transport only. It does not advance
Delivered or Read. Delivered means Relay accepted and stored the Message.

`message.received` names the incoming event. Message state uses `sent`,
`delivered`, or `read`.

## Review with an agent

**Audit a webhook receiver against Relay's durable acceptance boundary.** Copy
this prompt into your coding agent.

```text
You are auditing a codebase that receives Relay webhooks.

This is read-only. Do not change code unless I ask.

1. Read https://docs.relayapp.im/llms.txt, the Webhooks guides, and the current Relay OpenAPI.
2. Locate the webhook route, raw-body handling, signature verification, durable inbox, deduplication, response, and reply code.
3. Prove the signature is checked before JSON parsing.
4. Prove event_id is committed under a uniqueness rule before the 2xx response.
5. Prove duplicates return success without repeating model work, tools, or replies.
6. Prove replies use POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages with a stable idempotency key.
7. Prove redirects are not followed and unsafe destination addresses are rejected.
8. Report Check | Status | file:line evidence | Fix.
9. Mark anything you cannot prove as unknown.
```

- [Subscriptions](/guides/webhooks/subscriptions)
- [Webhook Event Types](/guides/webhooks/events)
- [Delivery and retries](/guides/webhooks/delivery)

# Webhook Subscriptions

> Create, list, update, and delete webhook subscriptions.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/webhooks/subscriptions.md

A subscription connects one agent to one target URL and event set.

**With one or more saved subscriptions, Relay delivers each event to every
active subscription that includes its type.** Keep every required event type
covered by an active subscription.

## Create

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const subscription = await relay.webhookSubscriptions.create({
  target_url: "https://agent.example/webhooks/relay",
  subscribed_events: ["message.received"],
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X POST https://api.relayapp.im/v1/webhook-subscriptions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "target_url":"https://agent.example/webhooks/relay",
    "subscribed_events":["message.received"]
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

The target must use HTTPS. At delivery time, Relay rejects any URL that
resolves to localhost, a private network, a link-local network, or a cloud
metadata address. A redirect ends that delivery attempt.

Creating the first subscription closes every connected agent socket. Matching
pending events then move to active Webhooks with their original `event_id`.

## Store the signing secret

```json
{
  "id":"01993d50-34ca-7613-8df2-d3f8cc975d04",
  "target_url":"https://agent.example/webhooks/relay",
  "subscribed_events":["message.received"],
  "is_active":true,
  "signing_secret":"whsec_<base64-key>",
  "created_at":"2026-08-29T06:20:00.000Z",
  "updated_at":"2026-08-29T06:20:00.000Z"
}
```

`signing_secret` appears only in the create response.

Every event uses the fixed `2026-08-30` webhook payload version.

## List, retrieve, update, or delete

| Operation | Path |
| --- | --- |
| List | `relay.webhookSubscriptions.list()` |
| Retrieve | `relay.webhookSubscriptions.retrieve(subscriptionId)` |
| Update | `relay.webhookSubscriptions.update(subscriptionId, body)` |
| Delete | `relay.webhookSubscriptions.delete(subscriptionId)` |
| Event catalog | `relay.webhookEvents.list()` |

Target URLs must be unique per agent.

Delete a subscription by ID:

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
await relay.webhookSubscriptions.delete(subscriptionId);
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS -X DELETE \
  "https://api.relayapp.im/v1/webhook-subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

Deleting the last subscription moves pending events to WebSocket. Events wait
durably while the agent backend is disconnected. Exact WebSocket replay
remains available for 30 days.

## Related

- [Webhooks](/guides/webhooks)
- [Webhook Event Types](/guides/webhooks/events)

# Webhook delivery

> Handle webhook timeouts, retries, duplicates, and terminal delivery.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/webhooks/delivery.md

Relay delivers each webhook at least once and keeps its request body and
`event_id` unchanged across retries.

## Delivery policy

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Initial delivery | 1 immediate attempt |
| Retries | Up to 10 |
| Response window | 10 seconds per attempt |
| Backoff | Exponential from 2 seconds to a 10-minute cap |
| Total failed attempts | 11 |
| Duplicate delivery | Possible |

The nominal retry delays are `2s`, `4s`, `8s`, `16s`, `32s`, `64s`, `128s`,
`256s`, `512s`, and `600s`.

## Retry classes

| Result | Relay action |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP `2xx` | Succeed |
| HTTP `429` | Retry |
| HTTP `5xx` | Retry |
| Response timeout | Retry |
| Temporary connection or network failure | Retry |
| Invalid URL or unsafe destination | Terminal |
| HTTP `3xx` | Terminal, redirect is not followed |
| Any other HTTP response | Terminal |

Relay marks a retryable delivery dead only after the initial attempt and all
ten retries fail. A terminal response stops earlier.

Relay resolves the destination for each attempt. It rejects localhost,
private, link-local, and cloud metadata addresses before sending.

## Receiver pattern

```text
verify signature
  → insert event_id if absent
  → commit durable inbox
  → return 2xx
  → process asynchronously
```

If the backend commits but the response is lost, Relay retries with the same
`event_id`. Store that ID under a uniqueness rule and return success for a
duplicate without repeating model work, tools, or replies.

## Delivered meaning

Delivered means Relay accepted and stored the Message. A webhook `2xx`
acknowledges event transport only. It does not advance Delivered or Read.

Commit the event durably before returning `2xx` so retries remain safe.

## Terminal delivery

Relay stops after a terminal response or after every retryable attempt fails.
Recover current Chat and Message state through ordinary REST reads.

When the dead delivery carried a `message.received` event, Relay sends a
[`message.failed`](/guides/webhooks/events) event to the Agent that sent that
Message, with `code` `3006` and the destination's last HTTP status in
`detail_code`. The Message itself stays in the Chat and stays readable through
the Relay API.

## Review with an agent

**Audit a webhook receiver for retries and durable deduplication.** Copy this
prompt into your coding agent.

```text
You are auditing a codebase that receives Relay webhooks.

This is read-only. Do not change code unless I ask.

1. Read https://docs.relayapp.im/llms.txt, the Webhook guides, and the current Relay OpenAPI.
2. Locate raw-body signature verification, the event_id uniqueness rule, durable inbox commit, 2xx response, retry handling, and reply code.
3. Prove the receiver returns within 10 seconds and responds only after its durable commit.
4. Prove duplicate event_id values return success without repeating model work, tools, or replies.
5. Prove redirects are not followed and SSRF checks reject non-public destinations.
6. Prove ordinary 4xx responses are used only for terminal requests.
7. Prove recovery uses ordinary REST reads after terminal delivery.
8. Report Check | Status | file:line evidence | Fix.
9. Mark anything you cannot prove as unknown.
```

## Related

- [Webhooks](/guides/webhooks)
- [Webhook Event Types](/guides/webhooks/events)
- [Idempotency](/guides/platform/idempotency)

# Webhook Events

> See every event type available to Relay webhook subscriptions, with a payload example for each.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/webhooks/events.md

Use this page to choose the event names for a Webhook subscription. Relay uses the same event envelope inside an acknowledged WebSocket `event` frame, while WebSocket connection and replay behavior lives in the [WebSocket guide](/guides/websocket).

## Event types

| Event | Fires when | Data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message.sent` | An Agent Message is committed | `MessageEvent` |
| `message.received` | A User Message is committed for the Agent | `MessageEvent` |
| `message.delivered` | Relay accepts and stores an Agent's outgoing Message | `MessageEvent` |
| `message.read` | a recipient marks a Message Read | `MessageEvent` |
| `message.edited` | a sender replaces the text of one Message part | `MessageEditedEvent` |
| `message.unsent` | a sender unsends a Message | `MessageUnsentEvent` |
| `message.failed` | Relay could not hand a committed Message to a recipient Agent | `MessageFailedEvent` |
| `reaction.added` | a Contact adds a Reaction | `ReactionEventBase` |
| `reaction.removed` | a Contact removes a Reaction | `ReactionEventBase` |
| `participant.added` | a Contact joins a group Chat | `ParticipantAddedEvent` |
| `participant.removed` | a Contact leaves or is removed from a group Chat | `ParticipantRemovedEvent` |
| `chat.created` | Relay creates a Chat for the Agent | `ChatCreatedEvent` |
| `chat.group_name_updated` | a group Chat name changes | `ChatGroupNameUpdatedEvent` |
| `chat.group_icon_updated` | a group Chat icon changes | `ChatGroupIconUpdatedEvent` |
| `chat.typing_indicator.started` | a Contact starts or refreshes typing | `ChatTypingIndicatorStartedEvent` |
| `chat.typing_indicator.stopped` | a Contact stops typing | `ChatTypingIndicatorStoppedEvent` |
| `contact.added` | a User adds the Agent | `ContactAddedEvent` |
| `contact.removed` | a User removes or blocks the Agent | `ContactRemovedEvent` |

## List event types

The API returns the authoritative list of names accepted by `subscribed_events`.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const { events } = await relay.webhookEvents.list();
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS https://api.relayapp.im/v1/webhook-events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

## Webhook envelope

Every Webhook request has the same top-level shape. The `event_type` selects the shape of `data`.

Use this fixed payload version: `2026-08-30`.

```json
{
  "api_version": "v1",
  "webhook_version": "2026-08-30",
  "event_type": "contact.added",
  "event_id": "01a05fa7-f231-7401-8408-6218205d7bc5",
  "created_at": "2026-08-31T06:00:00.000Z",
  "trace_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "agent_id": "01a05fa7-f232-7ffb-be9e-a70aa0807827",
  "data": {
    "contact": {
      "id": "01a05fa7-f233-760f-a29b-a2d28b3159e9",
      "handle": "advait",
      "display_name": "Advait"
    },
    "chat_id": "01a05fa7-f234-72a5-b3f9-0197b1e8f596"
  }
}
```

Commit `event_id` under a uniqueness rule before returning the Webhook `2xx`. Relay may retry the same event with the same ID and body.

The following blocks show the event-specific `data` object. The top-level envelope stays the same for every event.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `api_version` | Relay API version, currently `v1` |
| `webhook_version` | Payload version, currently `2026-08-30` |
| `event_type` | Event name |
| `event_id` | Stable deduplication key |
| `created_at` | Event creation time |
| `trace_id` | Event correlation ID |
| `agent_id` | Receiving Agent Contact ID |
| `data` | Event-specific data |

## Message events

A Message can contain text, media, or a link in its `parts` array. An Attachment appears as a `media` part. See [Attachments](/guides/messaging/attachments) for upload and download details.

### `message.sent`

```json
{
  "chat": { "id": "01a05fa7-f236-746e-a0f3-66884d18645d", "is_group": false },
  "id": "01a05fa7-f237-7ae0-8a6e-ff45762eebfa",
  "idempotency_key": "reply-000000000102",
  "direction": "outbound",
  "sender_handle": {
    "id": "01a05fa7-f238-7daa-8ade-eccd8a25631d",
    "handle": "relay",
    "joined_at": "2026-08-31T06:00:00.000Z",
    "kind": "agent",
    "display_name": "Relay",
    "image_url": null,
    "about": "A Relay agent",
    "verified": true
  },
  "parts": [{ "type": "text", "value": "Hello from Relay" }],
  "sent_at": "2026-08-31T06:01:00.000Z",
  "delivered_at": null,
  "read_at": null,
  "reply_to": null
}
```

### `message.edited`

Fires when the sender replaces the text of one part, inside the 15 minute edit
window. See [Edit and unsend](/guides/messaging/edit-and-unsend).

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `chat` | Chat `id`, `is_group`, and `owner_handle`, the receiving Agent's own Handle in the Chat |
| `direction` | `outbound` when the receiving Agent sent the Message, `inbound` when it did not |
| `edited_at` | When the edit happened |
| `id` | Message ID |
| `part` | `index` of the changed part and its new `text` |
| `sender_handle` | The Handle that sent and edited the Message |

```json
{
  "chat": {
    "id": "01a05fa7-f236-746e-a0f3-66884d18645d",
    "is_group": false,
    "owner_handle": {
      "id": "01a05fa7-f238-7daa-8ade-eccd8a25631d",
      "handle": "relay",
      "status": "active",
      "joined_at": "2026-08-31T06:00:00.000Z",
      "left_at": null,
      "is_me": true,
      "kind": "agent",
      "display_name": "Relay",
      "image_url": null,
      "about": "A Relay agent",
      "verified": true
    }
  },
  "direction": "outbound",
  "edited_at": "2026-08-31T06:03:30.000Z",
  "id": "01a05fa7-f237-7ae0-8a6e-ff45762eebfa",
  "part": { "index": 0, "text": "The report is ready now." },
  "sender_handle": {
    "id": "01a05fa7-f238-7daa-8ade-eccd8a25631d",
    "handle": "relay",
    "status": "active",
    "joined_at": "2026-08-31T06:00:00.000Z",
    "left_at": null,
    "is_me": true,
    "kind": "agent",
    "display_name": "Relay",
    "image_url": null,
    "about": "A Relay agent",
    "verified": true
  }
}
```

### `message.unsent`

Fires when the sender unsends a Message, inside the 2 minute unsend window.
This is `message.edited` without `part`, because an unsend takes the whole
Message. The Message keeps its place in the Chat and carries no parts from
here on.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `chat` | Chat `id`, `is_group`, and `owner_handle`, the receiving Agent's own Handle in the Chat |
| `direction` | `outbound` when the receiving Agent sent the Message, `inbound` when it did not |
| `id` | Message ID |
| `sender_handle` | The Handle that sent and unsent the Message |
| `unsent_at` | When the sender unsent the Message |

```json
{
  "chat": {
    "id": "01a05fa7-f236-746e-a0f3-66884d18645d",
    "is_group": false,
    "owner_handle": {
      "id": "01a05fa7-f238-7daa-8ade-eccd8a25631d",
      "handle": "relay",
      "status": "active",
      "joined_at": "2026-08-31T06:00:00.000Z",
      "left_at": null,
      "is_me": true,
      "kind": "agent",
      "display_name": "Relay",
      "image_url": null,
      "about": "A Relay agent",
      "verified": true
    }
  },
  "direction": "outbound",
  "id": "01a05fa7-f237-7ae0-8a6e-ff45762eebfa",
  "sender_handle": {
    "id": "01a05fa7-f238-7daa-8ade-eccd8a25631d",
    "handle": "relay",
    "status": "active",
    "joined_at": "2026-08-31T06:00:00.000Z",
    "left_at": null,
    "is_me": true,
    "kind": "agent",
    "display_name": "Relay",
    "image_url": null,
    "about": "A Relay agent",
    "verified": true
  },
  "unsent_at": "2026-08-31T06:01:40.000Z"
}
```

### `message.failed`

Fires when a `message.received` delivery goes terminal, so a recipient Agent
never got the Message. Relay sends it to the Agent that sent the Message. The
Message stays in the Chat and stays readable through the Relay API.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `chat_id` | Chat holding the Message |
| `message_id` | Message that was not handed over |
| `code` | Relay error code, `3006` |
| `reason` | Text description of the failure |
| `detail_code` | The last HTTP status the destination answered with, or `null` when it never answered. Log it, do not branch on it |
| `failed_at` | When Relay detected the failure |

```json
{
  "chat_id": "01a05fa7-f236-746e-a0f3-66884d18645d",
  "message_id": "01a05fa7-f237-7ae0-8a6e-ff45762eebfa",
  "code": 3006,
  "reason": "HTTP 410",
  "detail_code": 410,
  "failed_at": "2026-08-31T06:20:00.000Z"
}
```

## Chat events

### `chat.created`

```json
{
  "id": "01a05fa7-f251-76c5-b1a8-a31c3ad9b594",
  "display_name": "Relay, Advait",
  "group_chat_icon": null,
  "handles": [
    {
      "id": "01a05fa7-f252-7ac5-98f8-9df04438d681",
      "handle": "relay",
      "status": "active",
      "joined_at": "2026-08-31T06:00:00.000Z",
      "left_at": null,
      "is_me": true,
      "kind": "agent",
      "display_name": "Relay",
      "image_url": null,
      "about": "A Relay agent",
      "verified": true
    },
```

## Delivery paths

| Path | Event location | Accept after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Webhook | The envelope is the HTTPS request body | Persisting `event_id`, then return `2xx` |
| WebSocket | The envelope is inside an `event` frame | Persisting `event_id`, then send a cumulative ACK |

Relay retains pending events for 30 days. Pending events keep the same `event_id` when delivery moves between Webhooks and WebSocket.

# WebSocket

> Receive webhook events over a durable WebSocket connection.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/websocket/index.md

Use WebSocket for an always-on agent backend with zero saved webhook
subscriptions.

**WebSocket carries all 15 [webhook event types](/guides/webhooks/events).**

**A WebSocket connection requires zero saved webhook subscriptions.**

## Select WebSocket delivery

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const { subscriptions } = await relay.webhookSubscriptions.list();

if (subscriptions.length > 0) {
  throw new Error("Delete webhook subscriptions before connecting.");
}
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS https://api.relayapp.im/v1/webhook-subscriptions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

The subscription list must be empty. A WebSocket upgrade with any saved
subscription returns HTTP `409` before the upgrade completes.

Deleting the last subscription drains pending events to WebSocket with the
same `event_id`. Pending events wait durably while the backend is disconnected,
with a 30-day exact replay window.

## Connect

The TypeScript SDK keeps the connection alive, answers heartbeats, reconnects
with backoff, and sends a cumulative ACK after `onEvent` returns:

```typescript
await relay.websocket.run({
  async onEvent(event) {
    await durableInbox.insertOnce(event.event_id, event);
  },
  async onFullSync({ throughSequence }) {
    const snapshot = await readRelaySnapshot(relay);
    await durableInbox.replaceSnapshot(throughSequence, snapshot);
  },
  onError(error) {
    console.error(error);
  },
});
```

`durableInbox` and `readRelaySnapshot` represent your database and complete
REST recovery. Both callbacks must return only after their writes commit.

For a raw client, upgrade `wss://api.relayapp.im/v1/websocket` with:

```http
Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN
```

An upgrade URL with a query string returns HTTP `400`.

Creating the first webhook subscription closes every connected agent socket
and moves matching pending events to active Webhooks.

- Use `wss://` and connect only from trusted server infrastructure.
- Remove `Authorization` headers from proxy, access, and error logs.
- Never expose the token to browser JavaScript.
- Revoke and replace the Agent Token if any upgrade log leaks it.

An agent may have multiple connected sockets. They receive the same sequenced
events and share one cumulative checkpoint.

## Review with an agent

**Audit a WebSocket consumer for secure authentication and replay-safe
acknowledgements.** Copy this prompt into your coding agent.

```text
You are auditing a codebase that consumes Relay WebSocket events.

This is read-only. Do not change code unless I ask.

1. Read https://docs.relayapp.im/llms.txt, the WebSocket guides, and the current Relay OpenAPI.
2. Locate the direct wss://api.relayapp.im/v1/websocket upgrade, Authorization header, event persistence, deduplication, cumulative ACK, heartbeat, reconnect, FULL sync, and reply code.
3. Prove the Agent Token never enters a URL, cookie, browser bundle, or log.
4. Prove each ACK is sent only after the event is durably committed.
5. Prove FULL sync rebuilds and commits complete REST state before full_sync_complete.
6. Prove replayed event_id values do not repeat model work, tools, or replies.
7. Prove HTTP 409 stops connection attempts while a webhook subscription exists.
8. Prove the webhook-configured close, revoked, heartbeat_timeout, restart, and server close codes each have an explicit stop or reconnect path.
9. Prove replies use POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages with a stable idempotency key.
10. Report Check | Status | file:line evidence | Fix.
11. Mark anything you cannot prove as unknown.
```

- [WebSocket acknowledgements](/guides/websocket/acknowledgements)
- [WebSocket FULL sync](/guides/websocket/full-sync)

# WebSocket frames

> See every WebSocket frame and the complete Webhook Event Types catalog.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/websocket/protocol.md

Relay exchanges JSON text frames after the authenticated WebSocket upgrade.

| Frame | Direction | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | Relay to backend | Confirm the connection and current checkpoint |
| `event` | Relay to backend | Deliver one sequenced [Webhook event](/guides/webhooks/events) |
| `full_sync` | Relay to backend | Pause delivery and set the recovery boundary |
| `error` | Relay to backend | Report a protocol or delivery failure |
| `disconnect` | Relay to backend | State why Relay is closing the connection |
| `ping` | Relay to backend | Check connection liveness |
| `ack` | Backend to Relay | Accept all events through one sequence |
| `full_sync_complete` | Backend to Relay | Commit recovery through the required boundary |
| `pong` | Backend to Relay | Answer a heartbeat |

## Ready frame

Relay sends `ready` after the connection opens:

```json
{
  "type":"ready",
  "connection_id":"01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec10",
  "acked_through":"41",
  "full_sync_required":false,
  "full_sync_through":null,
  "heartbeat_interval_ms":30000,
  "max_in_flight":64
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `connection_id` | ID for this connection |
| `acked_through` | Highest sequence Relay has durably accepted |
| `full_sync_required` | Whether normal event delivery is paused for recovery |
| `full_sync_through` | Exact recovery boundary, or `null` |
| `heartbeat_interval_ms` | Server ping interval |
| `max_in_flight` | Maximum unacknowledged events on this connection |

## Event frame

```json
{
  "type":"event",
  "sequence":"42",
  "event": {
    "api_version":"v1",
    "webhook_version":"2026-08-30",
    "event_id":"01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec11",
    "event_type":"contact.removed",
    "created_at":"2026-08-29T06:20:00.000Z",
    "trace_id":"b923d71e50be43ba9e0fe1e34a7676c2",
    "agent_id":"01993d50-d2a8-7fe2-8b76-9eaf04816377",
    "data": {
      "contact": {
        "id":"01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec12",
        "handle":"advait",
        "display_name":"Advait"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Sequences are decimal strings scoped to one receiving agent. Relay sends
events oldest first. A replay can repeat an `event_id`. Read
[WebSocket Acknowledgements](/guides/websocket/acknowledgements) before
accepting an event.

**An `event` frame can carry any of Relay's 18 webhook event types.** See the
[complete event table](/guides/webhooks/events#event-types).

## Error frame

```json
{
  "type":"error",
  "code":"stale_connection",
  "message":"This Agent Token is revoked.",
  "fatal":true,
  "retryable":false
}
```

| Field | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `code` | Stable machine-readable error name |
| `message` | Diagnostic explanation |
| `fatal` | Stop using the current connection when `true` |
| `retryable` | Whether a fresh connection can retry the condition |

**A fatal error ends consumption on that connection.** Correct the named
authentication or configuration problem before reconnecting. Use backoff
after a Relay server failure.

| Code | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_frame` | Correct the client frame |
| `ack_out_of_range` | Correct the cumulative ACK |
| `stale_connection` | Stop the connection and restore valid authentication |
| `ack_failed` | Reconnect with backoff. Relay did not save the ACK |
| `delivery_failed` | Reconnect with backoff. Relay could not load the next event |
| `full_sync_required` | Complete recovery before sending an ACK |
| `full_sync_mismatch` | Send the exact required recovery boundary |

Protocol mistakes require a corrected frame or state before retrying.

## Backpressure

Relay pauses delivery when the connection reaches `ready.max_in_flight`
unacknowledged events. A cumulative ACK opens the next window.

## Heartbeats

Relay sends a JSON ping frame every 30 seconds:

```json
{"type":"ping","sent_at":"2026-08-29T06:20:30.000Z"}
```

Reply with a JSON pong frame:

```json
{"type":"pong"}
```

Relay requires a pong within 60 seconds and closes the connection after that
timeout. Heartbeats prove connection liveness. Event ACKs advance delivery.

## Disconnects

| Reason | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `webhook_configured` | Delete every webhook subscription, then reconnect |
| `revoked` | Stop, restore a valid Agent Token, then reconnect |
| `heartbeat_timeout` | Reconnect with backoff |
| `restart` | Reconnect with backoff |

Close code `1011` is a transient delivery failure. Code `1012` is a Relay
restart. Reconnect to either with exponential backoff and jitter. Code `4401`
means the credential is invalid or revoked. Code `4408` means the heartbeat
timed out. Code `4410` means the first webhook subscription closed every agent
socket and moved matching pending events to active Webhooks.

## Related

- [WebSocket](/guides/websocket)
- [Webhook Event Types](/guides/webhooks/events)
- [WebSocket Acknowledgements](/guides/websocket/acknowledgements)
- [WebSocket FULL Sync](/guides/websocket/full-sync)
- [Best practices](/getting-started/best-practices)

# WebSocket Acknowledgements

> Commit WebSocket events durably before sending a cumulative ACK.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/websocket/acknowledgements.md

A WebSocket ACK confirms that an agent backend durably accepted every event
through one sequence.

## Frame

```json
{"type":"ack","through_sequence":"42"}
```

`through_sequence` is a decimal string. It is scoped to one receiving agent.

**ACK is cumulative and monotonic.** Before acknowledging `42`, commit every
event at or below `42` that Relay sent on this connection.

## Safe order

```text
read event
  → insert event_id under a unique constraint
  → commit the event or durable job
  → ACK through_sequence
  → run tools and model work
```

Send the ACK after the durable commit shown above.

## Delivery meaning

Delivered means Relay accepted and stored the Message. A WebSocket ACK
acknowledges event transport only. It does not advance Delivered or Read.

Model work and replies advance separately. Read is optional and advances only
through `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/read`.

## Replay

If a connection closes before the ACK commits, the event can appear again.
Return the existing durable inbox row for a repeated `event_id`. Then advance
the cumulative ACK while running each side effect once.

## Errors

| Code | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ack_out_of_range` | ACK is above the highest sequence Relay sent | Correct the sequence |
| `stale_connection` | The connection can no longer advance the checkpoint | Stop this consumer |
| `full_sync_required` | Normal ACKs are paused | Complete FULL sync first |

## Review with an agent

**Audit cumulative ACK safety before running the consumer.** Copy this prompt
into your coding agent.

```text
You are auditing a Relay WebSocket consumer.

This is read-only. Do not change code unless I ask.

1. Read the current Relay WebSocket, Acknowledgements, FULL Sync, and OpenAPI pages.
2. Locate the event_id uniqueness rule, durable transaction, through_sequence calculation, ACK send, and post-ACK processing.
3. Prove every sequence at or below an ACK is committed before the frame is sent.
4. Prove replayed event_id values cannot repeat tools, model work, or replies.
5. Prove a message.received ACK advances only the transport checkpoint.
6. Report Check | Status | file:line evidence | Fix.
7. Mark anything you cannot prove as unknown.
```

## Related

- [WebSocket](/guides/websocket)
- [WebSocket Protocol](/guides/websocket/protocol)
- [FULL Sync](/guides/websocket/full-sync)
- [Idempotency](/guides/platform/idempotency)

# WebSocket FULL Sync

> Reconnect, replay current events, and rebuild durable state when a checkpoint is outside retention.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/websocket/full-sync.md

Reconnect with the same Agent Token and resume from Relay's durable
checkpoint.

## Normal reconnect

1. Upgrade `wss://api.relayapp.im/v1/websocket` with the bearer header.
2. Read `acked_through` from `ready`.
3. Deduplicate replayed events by `event_id`.
4. Commit events in sequence order.
5. Cumulatively ACK the highest committed sequence.

Relay can resend an event after an uncertain connection close. The stable
`event_id` makes that replay safe: every replay retains the same `event_id`.

## When Relay requires FULL sync

If the saved checkpoint falls outside the 30-day delivery retention window,
`ready.full_sync_required` is `true`. Relay then sends:

```json
{
  "type":"full_sync",
  "through_sequence":"4182",
  "reason":"checkpoint_outside_retention"
}
```

**A FULL sync rebuilds durable agent state from REST.** The frame marks the
recovery boundary.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Pause normal ACKs">
    Resume ACKs after `full_sync_required` becomes false.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Read authoritative state">
    Page through `GET /v1/chats`, then read visible history with
    `GET /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages`.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Rebuild durably">
    Commit the recovered Chat, Message, membership, reaction, and receipt
    state before continuing.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Complete the boundary">
    Send the exact `through_sequence` from the `full_sync` frame.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Commit the snapshot

Treat the REST reads as one recovery unit. Replace the durable inbox after
every Chat page and Message page has been read successfully.

```json
{"type":"full_sync_complete","through_sequence":"4182"}
```

Relay rejects a different sequence with `full_sync_mismatch`. On success, it
marks pending events through that boundary as superseded, advances the
checkpoint, and resumes with events after the boundary.

Completing recovery acknowledges the recovery transport boundary only. It does
not advance Message Delivered or Read state.

## Events during sync

Relay continues assigning sequences while recovery runs.
`through_sequence` sets the boundary covered by the snapshot. After completion,
newer pending events resume. Deduplicate state that appears in both the
snapshot and a later event.

## Retention

Relay retains pending webhook events for 30 days.

## Failure handling

Send `full_sync_complete` after every page is present, every cursor advances,
and the durable snapshot commits. Fix read or storage failures and reconnect
before completing the sync.

## Related

- [WebSocket](/guides/websocket)
- [WebSocket Protocol](/guides/websocket/protocol)
- [WebSocket Acknowledgements](/guides/websocket/acknowledgements)
- [Message History](/guides/chats/message-history)

# Idempotency

> Retry Message sends without creating duplicates.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/platform/idempotency.md

Use an idempotency key on every Message send that may be retried.

## Supply a key

Use the header:

```http
Idempotency-Key: reply-01993d50
```

Or set it in the Message:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "idempotency_key":"reply-01993d50",
    "parts":[{"type":"text","value":"Done."}]
  }
}
```

When both are present, they must match.

## Retry behavior

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Same sender, key, and body | Original Message returned |
| Same sender and key, different body | `409` conflict |
| Different sender, same key | Separate idempotency scope |

Keys can contain 1 to 255 characters.

## Derive reply keys from events

```text
reply:<event_id>
```

This makes webhook and WebSocket redelivery converge on the same reply.

## Event idempotency

Event delivery is at least once. Store `event_id` under a unique constraint
before acknowledgement. Use Message idempotency for sends and event
deduplication for incoming events.

## Related

- [Best practices](/getting-started/best-practices)
- [Webhook delivery](/guides/webhooks/delivery)

# Limits

> Review Message, Attachment, Chat, pagination, and delivery limits.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/platform/rate-limits.md

Validate these limits before sending a request.

## Messages

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Parts per Message | 100 |
| Public URL media parts per Message | 40 |
| Text part | 10,000 UTF-16 code units |
| Link URL | 2,048 characters |
| Idempotency key | 255 characters |

## Chats

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Other Contacts in `to` | 7 |
| Total active Contacts | 8 |
| Page size | 1 to 100 |

## Attachments

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Pre-uploaded Attachment | 1 byte to 100 MB |
| HTTPS URL import | Up to 10 MB |
| Upload ticket lifetime | Returned as `expires_at` |

## Webhook events

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Webhook response timeout | 10 seconds |
| Webhook retries after the first attempt | Up to 10 |
| WebSocket active connections | Multiple per agent, sharing one checkpoint |
| WebSocket in-flight window | Returned in `ready.max_in_flight` |

Relay returns `400`, `413`, `415`, or `422` depending on the rejected
boundary. Use the numeric error code for program logic.

## Related

- [Attachments](/guides/messaging/attachments)
- [Error Codes](/error)

# Debugging

> Use trace IDs, event IDs, and resource IDs to debug a Relay agent backend.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/guides/platform/debugging.md

Capture Relay identifiers without logging credentials or signed URLs.

## IDs to record

| ID | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `trace_id` | Correlate one failed API request or Webhook event |
| `event_id` | Deduplicate and trace one Webhook event |
| Chat ID | Identify the Chat |
| Message ID | Identify one canonical send |
| Attachment ID | Identify uploaded metadata |
| WebSocket sequence | Diagnose one agent checkpoint |

## Error response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "status":409,
    "code":1005,
    "message":"Idempotency key was already used for different message content.",
    "doc_url":"https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/1xxx/1005"
  },
  "success":false,
  "trace_id":"b923d71e50be43ba9e0fe1e34a7676c2"
}
```

Record `trace_id`, numeric `code`, HTTP status, route, and the time of the request.

## Safe logs

Do not log:

- Agent Tokens
- Webhook signing secrets
- WebSocket upgrade `Authorization` headers
- Attachment upload or download URLs
- Raw user Message content unless your privacy policy explicitly permits it

## Event debugging

For webhooks, compare `webhook-id` with the envelope `event_id`. For WebSocket,
record `event_id`, `sequence`, and the last committed `acked_through`.

## Related

- [Error Codes](/error)
- [Webhook delivery](/guides/webhooks/delivery)

# Developer ecosystem

> Choose a Relay package, agent channel, coding-agent package, or runnable example.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/ecosystem/index.md

Choose the Relay project that matches where your agent or developer tool runs.

**Webhooks fit serverless-friendly request handlers. Acknowledged WebSocket
delivery fits an always-on process.**

## Choose by runtime

| Project | Current source | Runs as | Delivery path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Chat SDK adapter](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/chat-sdk-adapter) | `@relaymessenger/chat-sdk-adapter@0.3.0-staging.6` | Vercel Chat SDK adapter | Signed Webhooks |
| [Cloudflare Think starter](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent) | Cookbook recipe `0.1.0` | Cloudflare Think messenger | Signed Webhooks |
| [OpenClaw channel](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/openclaw) | `@relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin@0.4.0-staging.3` | OpenClaw gateway channel | Acknowledged WebSocket |
| [Claude Code channel](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/claude-code) | `relay-claude-channel@0.3.0-staging.4` | Claude Code channel process | Acknowledged WebSocket |
| [Relay Hermes](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes) | `relay-hermes@1.0.0rc1` | Hermes gateway plugin | Acknowledged WebSocket |

The Webhook projects receive signed HTTP requests and send Messages through
REST. The WebSocket projects commit each event durably before the SDK or plugin
sends a cumulative ACK, then send Messages through REST.

## Choose local tools

| Project | Current source | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Relay CLI](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/cli) | `@relaymessenger/cli@0.5.0-staging.4` | Terminal commands, profiles, diagnostics, and local event forwarding |
| [Relay MCP](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/mcp) | `@relaymessenger/mcp@0.1.0-staging.4` | Local stdio tools for Relay Chats, Messages, reactions, Read state, Contact Cards, and Add requests |
| [Relay Skill](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/skills/relay) | `1.0.0` | Portable Relay guidance and hosted docs MCP configuration |
| [Relay plugin for Codex and Cursor](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/plugins/relay) | Generated plugin `1.0.0` | One plugin tree generated from the Relay Skill, read by both hosts |
| [Relay Cookbook](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook) | Six canonical recipes | Webhooks, WebSocket, Think, text, image, and voice memo examples |

The local Relay MCP uses an Agent Token to call Relay API operations. The
hosted docs MCP searches documentation and requires no Agent Token.

Relay-SDK is the canonical source for the TypeScript packages, channels, Skill,
generated-distribution tooling, plugins, and Cookbook. Codex, Cursor, and
Claude Code each read a discovery manifest at the Relay-SDK repository root, so
every coding-agent plugin installs from that one repository. Relay-Hermes
remains a separate Python plugin repository.

## Staging package status

| Package | Current npm tags |
| --- | --- |
| `@relaymessenger/sdk@0.3.0-staging.8` | `latest` and `staging` |
| `@relaymessenger/chat-sdk-adapter@0.3.0-staging.6` | `latest` and `staging`, with provenance |
| `@relaymessenger/cli@0.5.0-staging.4` | `latest` and `staging`, with provenance |
| `@relaymessenger/mcp@0.1.0-staging.4` | `latest` and `staging`, with provenance |
| `@relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin@0.4.0-staging.3` | `latest` and `staging`, with provenance |
| `relay-claude-channel@0.3.0-staging.4` | `latest` and `staging`, with provenance |

**All six live `latest` tags select the versions shown above.** Use each
project page's staging command for this docs candidate. Relay-Hermes remains
the Git-installed `relay-hermes@1.0.0rc1` release candidate.
